candidates.lead: Lewis Rimmer was in an induced coma after being hit by a car and suffering life-changing injuries
candidates.evidence_text: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket - BBC News Image source, Sarah Rimmer Image caption, Sarah and Lewis Rimmer, pictured with their daughters, have vowed to stay positive By Lauren Hirst North West Published 1 November 2026 Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night. Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in the car park of a Sainsbury's store in Bolton, Greater Manchester - just moments after he bought a lottery ticket. The doting father was airlifted to the Royal Preston Hospital where his family were told he had just a 30% chance of pulling through. Lewis spent weeks on life support and had more than 40 hours of surgery, including the amputation of his left foot. "For three weeks, I couldn't hear his voice, tell him about the girls or ask him for advice," said Sarah, reflecting on how life had changed one year on. "The girls couldn't understand why we couldn't Facetime daddy." Image source, Sarah Rimmer Image caption, Lewis Rimmer had been with his wife and two daughters shortly before he was hit In the following three weeks, medics reduced the sedation and each day Sarah would hope to hear the words "settled overnight", indicating he had progressed and was comfortable. "The next six weeks brought a whole new battle," she said. "Waking up, piecing together what had happened, learning to eat and drink again and slowly seeing the tubes and machines disappear. "The girls finally got to see their daddy and began to understand what had actually gone on." On the day of the incident on 27 October 2025, Lewis had taken the afternoon off work to celebrate the birthday of his eldest daughter. Image source, Sarah Rimmer Image caption, Lewis missed his older daughter's birthday while in hospital Driving straight from the car garage where he works, he met his wife and their two daughters at a cafe close to their Bolton home. He was hit just minutes after buying the lottery ticket and waving goodbye to his family. Lewis was left with a broken pelvis, fractures to both femurs, a compound fracture to his right shin and severe damage to his left foot, which could not be saved. Six months after the crash, Lewis was finally able to go home. Sarah said the family now faced "a completely different life" and "a long road to recovery" but were determined to stay positive. "We're busy with appointments but it's all positive things moving forward," she said. "It's just a new journey that we're doing now, navigating everything." A 57-year-old man is due to stand trial in November after being charged with causing serious injury by dangerous driving. candidates.evidence_text: Christmas lights switch-ons across the North West in 2026 - BBC News Image source, Mark Waugh Image caption, Events will take place across the region to mark the start of the countdown to Christmas By Lauren Hirst North West Published 1 November 2026 It's beginning to look a lot like Christmas in north-west England, as towns and cities in the region light up for the festive season. As the countdown to 25 December begins, cities and towns across the region have set the date to switch on their Christmas lights, marking the start of the yuletide festivities. Below are confirmed details of when and where events are taking place locally. Merseyside Southport: The annual ceremony takes place on Saturday 7 November, with free entertainment outside The Grand and performances from Regally Royal Parties from 16:00 GMT. Huyton: The Christmas lights switch-on will take place in the village centre from 15:00 to 19:00 on Friday 13 November. Prescot: The Christmas lights switch-on will take place in the town centre from 15:00 until 19:00 on Saturday 14 November. Kirkby: The Christmas lights switch-on will take place in the town centre from 16:30 to 19:30 on Friday 20 November. Greater Manchester Manchester: There will not be an official Christmas lights switch-on in Manchester, but the lights will be turned on across the city on Friday 6 November. Bury: The Rock Shopping Centre is marking its 15th year with a new tradition - its first Christmas parade and lights switch-on, on Saturday 7 November. Festivities start from 16:00 where visitors are asked to meet for the parade. Oldham: The Christmas lights switch-on will be held on Saturday 14 November, starting with meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles Kids Club from 13:00. Celebrations will feature Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance, followed by fireworks and a lights and laser show from 17:30. Tameside: The Northern Lights Lantern Parade in Ashton returns on Saturday 14 November, setting off at 17:00 and wrapping up with a festive light switch-on at about 18:30. Stockport: More than 200 performers and 50 free shows are set to take over the town centre on Sunday 15 November from 12:00 to 17:00, followed by a parade featuring more than 100 drummers, with the Christmas lights switch-on at 16:45. Rochdale: The Christmas lights switch-on will take place on Sunday 22 November at 17:30 in front of the town hall following a countdown. Ignite Fire Festival continues opposite Rochdale Town Hall until 20:00. Image source, Mark Waugh Image caption, Light displays will be on show across the region Lancashire Burnley: Enjoy a variety of activities from 12:00 on St James's Street. The magical lantern parade starts at about 16:00, followed by the lights switch-on at 17:00, on Saturday 14 November. Darwen: The Christmas lights switch-on will be held at Darwen Market Square on Saturday 14 November. The timings have not yet been confirmed. West Lancashire: Lighting up the festive season first will be Skelmersdale on Sunday 15 November at 17:00, followed by Ormskirk on Sunday 22 November, also at 17:00. Street performers, charity stalls, fairground rides and artisan market stalls will also be on hand to sprinkle some Christmas magic for all ages to enjoy earlier in the day. Preston: The Christmas lights switch-on event returns to the Flag Market, with East 17 headlining an evening of live music and entertainment on Saturday 21 November from 17:30. Leyland: Singer-songwriter Aston Merrygold will be turning on Leyland's Christmas lights on Saturday 28 November, at 17:30 on Hough Lane. The Christmas markets will open at 12:00, with stage entertainment from 13:30. Lancaster: The Christmas lights switch-on will be held on Sunday 29 November. The timings have not yet been confirmed. Cheshire Wilmslow: The countdown to flip the switch on Wilmslow's Christmas lights begins at 17:00 on Saturday 21 November. The markets will open from 10:00 on Alderley Road with on-stage entertainment from 13:30. Sandbach: The Christmas lights switch-on will be held on Saturday 28 November from 15:00 to 18:00 on the Cobbles. Crewe: The build-up to Crewe's Christmas lights switch-on begins at 14:00 on Saturday 28 November. New details of other Christmas lights switch-ons can be emailed to northwestonline@bbc.co.uk. candidates.lead: The NHS says rates have improved, but that too many women are still not getting checked
candidates.evidence_text: Over a quarter of eligible women in the North West are missing breast cancer screening appointments The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 50 and 53, then every three years after that until they are 71 Dr Paula Cowan, a GP and the regional medical director for primary care at NHS England in the North West, said "some people may be reluctant to come forward for a number of different reasons" but that "breast screening... detect cancer at an early stage" The NHS encourages women to continue to check their breasts regularly and to get any unusual changes to how they look and feel checked out by their GP Tell us which stories we should cover in the North West

candidates.evidence_text: A former football club chief executive has pleaded guilty to offences relating to the drugging and raping of a woman by her husband and others Karl Lindsay, 56, who resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged, has admitted the offences, which happened between 2015 and 2025 Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard Lindsay's offending related to the rape of the woman by her husband and others in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, and the administration of substances to stupefy her for the purpose of sexual acts The woman's husband, who is in his 60s and cannot be named to protect his wife's anonymity, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife, including rape The woman at the centre of the case was in court with one of her relatives and watched Lindsay intently as he entered his guilty pleas Three other men, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee, Scotland, Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport, and Graham Brougham, 74, from Northwich, have already admitted sexually abusing her at previous hearings

candidates.lead: Manchester could get its first Black city-centre statue after years of campaigning
candidates.evidence_text: He was one of Britain's best boxers, but never became champion Born in Clayton, Manchester, in 1902, Len Johnson won more than 90 fights during his career but was barred from contesting the British title because of the colour of his skin He later channelled the fighting spirit he showed in the ring into campaigning against racism, becoming a trade unionist, civil rights activist and member of the Communist Party More than 50 years after his death, Johnson is set to become the first black person to be honoured with a statue in Manchester. But who was Len Johnson? Despite having little boxing knowledge or training, he got his first taste of the sport after a fight at work prompted his father, a former boxer, to take him to a local contest A few weeks later, after training by skipping with an old washing line, he stepped into the ring for his first bout at the Alhambra Theatre in Openshaw

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Warning: This article contains distressing content A man has been found guilty of murdering a head teacher who was dragged to his death for more than a mile while trapped under the wheels of a car Simon Richardson crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was cycling home from his job at Stretford Grammar School on the evening of 20 April in the village of Warburton in Trafford, Greater Manchester Prosecutors claimed Richardson, 35, fled the scene of the crash before stopping to try to dislodge the injured but still-living cyclist and then driving on with Mr Mullins still lodged underneath the vehicle Richardson was also convicted of dangerous driving and will return to Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court to be sentenced on Monday There were shouts of "Yes!" from the court's public gallery as the guilty murder verdict was announced

candidates.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

candidates.evidence_text: A former football club chief executive has pleaded guilty to offences relating to the drugging and raping of a woman by her husband and others Karl Lindsay, 56, who resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged, has admitted the offences, which happened between 2015 and 2025 Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard Lindsay's offending related to the rape of the woman by her husband and others in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, and the administration of substances to stupefy her for the purpose of sexual acts The woman's husband, who is in his 60s and cannot be named to protect his wife's anonymity, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife, including rape The woman at the centre of the case was in court with one of her relatives and watched Lindsay intently as he entered his guilty pleas Three other men, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee, Scotland, Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport, and Graham Brougham, 74, from Northwich, have already admitted sexually abusing her at previous hearings

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre 'Significant disruption' across Manchester amid MORE traffic chaos Repairs are continuing on the major bus route in Manchester city centre amid Portland Street leak Add to preferred sources Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and b 'Significant disruption' in Manchester city centre is continuing this week after a water main burst on a major bus route Portland Street was first closed off after the main pipe burst on the road on Wednesday (October 28). A large cordon was put in place around the area as United Utilities began repair work The incident led to traffic chaos around the city centre and the closure of Piccadilly Gardens bus station, which caused hours worth of delays for commuters over the weekend. Today (Monday, November 2) Portland Street will remain closed while repair works go on The bus station will also remain shut, according to the Bee Network website. The website states: "A water leak on Portland Street is causing significant disruption in the city centre "Portland Street and Piccadilly Gardens will be closed on Monday 2 November while work takes to repair the pipe. This is affecting the following bus services which use Portland Street and Piccadilly Gardens: 15, 18, 30, 33, 38, 41, 42, 42A, 42B, 42C, 43, 50, 85, 85A, 86, 87, 101

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The knife attacks that have rocked the Arndale SPECIAL REPORT: As Manchester prepares for the festive shopping rush under the shadow of three knife-related incidents in just 11 days, shoppers share their fears while police surge Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter , Eva Millett and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 05:56, 02 Nov 2026 As monsters perch on top of buildings and familiar wooden huts spring up across town , Manchester stands on the eve of its busiest shopping season. But Police stormed and surrounded the Manchester Arndale on three occasions in 11 days. It followed three knife-related incidents, which Greater Manchester Police does not believe to be linked to one another With the city's streets and shopping centres set to become ever busier as the weeks tick along before Christmas , some shoppers told the Manchester Evening News they feel 'nervous'. The incidents began with a 14-year-old boy stabbed on the ninth level of the multi-storey car park Witnesses reported seeing several people run from the shopping centre to the car park moments before the attack. Armed officers were soon in attendance on High Street, Withy Grove and Dantzic Street close to the Arndale, while shoppers' cars were kept inside a cordon for hours in Quick-thinking passers-by were praised by Greater Manchester Police for saving the young victim from life-threatening injuries. Two 14-year-old boys were arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and later released on bail

candidates.evidence_text: Salford The true Salford giant and dapper union man who strove for a better city Bill Moores, who dedicated his life 'to serving others and tirelessly fighting injustice', has died, aged 84 View 5 Images During the strike of 1984–85, Bill forged Salfo Add to preferred sources News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:57, 01 Nov 2026 In the late 1980s, Salford was desolate and bleak in parts, and brave decisions were required. It needed partnerships with private developers and talks with a Tory government But through it all Bill Moores stayed true to his roots. He became a key man in Labour's leadership as it got to grips with regeneration into the early 1990s He was deputy to Salford Council leader, Bill Hinds, when - thanks to the foresight of planning boss, councillor Ben Wallsworth - a shattered city showed signs of rising again Ben, previous council leader Les Hough, and then-chief executive Roger Rees, were the architects of a gamble. It was one that would transform the city and its reputation In an agreement finalised behind closed doors, the council decided to pay £1m for the city's desolate docklands, which had once been the spine of the city's economy. That decision would not only create Salford Quays - but help cement Greater Manchester's reputation as the foremos

Called a Local Plan, it is a key document produced by councils outlining a vision for their boroughs and a roadmap for develo Stockport council is currently asking for public feedback on plans before a likely submission in the next few months. While town hall bosses believe the plan is legally sound, it is still around 8,000 homes short of the housing targets set by the UK Government The government says its approach to housing is aimed at tackling a housing crisis as ‘too many people are being priced out of the communities where they want to live and work’. However in High Lane on the edge of the Peak District, fears are growing that a rural village of less t Under the draft Local Plan, 1,000 homes could be built to the north and south of the A6 which cuts through the village. A Persimmon Homes planning application is also being considered to the north for over 200 homes off Windlehurst Road

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The knife attacks that have rocked the Arndale SPECIAL REPORT: As Manchester prepares for the festive shopping rush under the shadow of three knife-related incidents in just 11 days, shoppers share their fears while police surge Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter , Eva Millett and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 05:56, 02 Nov 2026 As monsters perch on top of buildings and familiar wooden huts spring up across town , Manchester stands on the eve of its busiest shopping season. But Police stormed and surrounded the Manchester Arndale on three occasions in 11 days. It followed three knife-related incidents, which Greater Manchester Police does not believe to be linked to one another With the city's streets and shopping centres set to become ever busier as the weeks tick along before Christmas , some shoppers told the Manchester Evening News they feel 'nervous'. The incidents began with a 14-year-old boy stabbed on the ninth level of the multi-storey car park Witnesses reported seeing several people run from the shopping centre to the car park moments before the attack. Called a Local Plan, it is a key document produced by councils outlining a vision for their boroughs and a roadmap for develo Stockport council is currently asking for public feedback on plans before a likely submission in the next few months. While town hall bosses believe the plan is legally sound, it is still around 8,000 homes short of the housing targets set by the UK Government The government says its approach to housing is aimed at tackling a housing crisis as ‘too many people are being priced out of the communities where they want to live and work’. However in High Lane on the edge of the Peak District, fears are growing that a rural village of less t Under the draft Local Plan, 1,000 homes could be built to the north and south of the A6 which cuts through the village. A Persimmon Homes planning application is also being considered to the north for over 200 homes off Windlehurst Road

There are no rays of autumn sunshine. But I am still optimisitic I am checking out a sanctuary next to a gently gurgling stream. Sadly any hope of quiet contemplation is shattered by a cacophony of children It is half term and Britain's fifth national garden is a natural destination for young families. A path to the new attraction at RHS Bridgewater in Worsley is the one I am taking It cost £1.8m and is meant to radiate peace and serenity. Twenty containers of authentic materials were shipped from China to create it. This included Fir timber used to make traditional hand-crafted mortise-and-tenon joinery and kiln-fired tiles and handmade brickwork from the s It is the Yangzhou Scholar's Garden and in old China they were found within city walls as the Ming dynasty was eclipsed by the Qing from 1644 to 1912. candidates.summary: Manchester City Centre The knife attacks that have rocked the Arndale SPECIAL REPORT: As Manchester prepares for the festive shopping rush under the shadow of three knife-related incidents in just 11 days, shoppers share their fears while police surge Add to preferred sources New

candidates.lead: Manchester City Centre The knife attacks that have rocked the Arndale SPECIAL REPORT: As Manchester prepares for the festive shopping rush under the shadow of three knife-related incidents in just 11 days, shoppers share their fears while police surge Add to preferred sources New
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The knife attacks that have rocked the Arndale SPECIAL REPORT: As Manchester prepares for the festive shopping rush under the shadow of three knife-related incidents in just 11 days, shoppers share their fears while police surge Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter , Eva Millett and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 05:56, 02 Nov 2026 As monsters perch on top of buildings and familiar wooden huts spring up across town , Manchester stands on the eve of its busiest shopping season. But Police stormed and surrounded the Manchester Arndale on three occasions in 11 days. It followed three knife-related incidents, which Greater Manchester Police does not believe to be linked to one another With the city's streets and shopping centres set to become ever busier as the weeks tick along before Christmas , some shoppers told the Manchester Evening News they feel 'nervous'. The incidents began with a 14-year-old boy stabbed on the ninth level of the multi-storey car park Witnesses reported seeing several people run from the shopping centre to the car park moments before the attack. Armed officers were soon in attendance on High Street, Withy Grove and Dantzic Street close to the Arndale, while shoppers' cars were kept inside a cordon for hours in Quick-thinking passers-by were praised by Greater Manchester Police for saving the young victim from life-threatening injuries. Two 14-year-old boys were arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and later released on bail

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester weather Greater Manchester no longer in drought as Met Office issues Bonfire Night forecast After a week of heavy rain the north west is in 'receovery status' but it looks we're in for a dry week ahead Add to preferred sources News Damon Wi Mostly dry conditions are forecast for the week ahead, despite Greater Manchester no longer being in drought conditions, forecasters have said. High pressure is to bring mostly settled weather to the north west the Met Office say, which is good news for Bonfire Night After being in drought for much of the summer, all of north-west England, including Greater Manchester and Cumbria , was moved to recovery status on Wednesday, after England experienced its wettest week for two years, the Environment Agency (EA) said. But, severe drought remains Much of Wales also remains in drought after the UK's hottest summer since records began in 1884. At least 120% of average rainfall is needed over the next six months for the entire country to be out of drought by next spring, the EA said Tom Morgan, meteorologist at the Met Office, said: "High pressure will dominate, which is still unfortunately bad news for southern regions in particular, which are experiencing the severe drought conditions that we've seen for several months now. There may well be a few showers "But for all other parts of the UK, it's largely going to be dry."

High pressure is to bring mostly settled weather to the north west the Met Office say, which is good news for Bonfire Night After being in drought for much of the summer, all of north-west England, including Greater Manchester and Cumbria , was moved to recovery status on Wednesday, after England experienced its wettest week for two years, the Environment Agency (EA) said. But, severe drought remains Much of Wales also remains in drought after the UK's hottest summer since records began in 1884. At least 120% of average rainfall is needed over the next six months for the entire country to be out of drought by next spring, the EA said Tom Morgan, meteorologist at the Met Office, said: "High pressure will dominate, which is still unfortunately bad news for southern regions in particular, which are experiencing the severe drought conditions that we've seen for several months now. It needed partnerships with private developers and talks with a Tory government But through it all Bill Moores stayed true to his roots. He became a key man in Labour's leadership as it got to grips with regeneration into the early 1990s He was deputy to Salford Council leader, Bill Hinds, when - thanks to the foresight of planning boss, councillor Ben Wallsworth - a shattered city showed signs of rising again Ben, previous council leader Les Hough, and then-chief executive Roger Rees, were the architects of a gamble. It was one that would transform the city and its reputation In an agreement finalised behind closed doors, the council decided to pay £1m for the city's desolate docklands, which had once been the spine of the city's economy. While town hall bosses believe the plan is legally sound, it is still around 8,000 homes short of the housing targets set by the UK Government The government says its approach to housing is aimed at tackling a housing crisis as ‘too many people are being priced out of the communities where they want to live and work’. However in High Lane on the edge of the Peak District, fears are growing that a rural village of less t Under the draft Local Plan, 1,000 homes could be built to the north and south of the A6 which cuts through the village. A Persimmon Homes planning application is also being considered to the north for over 200 homes off Windlehurst Road

The footage has been seen by tens of thousands of social media users in recent Two widely-circulated posts which accompanied the clip claimed the video showed 'a full street of houses emptied for illegal immigrants to be moved in'. Most of the properties have their lights switched off, with only a small number of the houses seemingly occupied A woman with a local accent can be heard narrating the footage. At one point, she turns the camera to either end of the street, to highlight the proximity to Ordsall Park at one end and Primrose Hill Primary School at the other She tells viewers: "Did you know, on Ordsall, that they’ve emptied all these out for all the immigrants to be moving in them? Following two weeks of evidence, jurors Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:32, 01 Nov 2026 Only two people know exactly what happened in the Volvo that hit Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins as he was dragged more than a mile down the road to his death One wept as she gave evidence from a Crown Court witness box, shielded by a screen. The other faces a life sentence for murder Beloved educator and dad-of-two Mr Mullins was killed in horrific circumstances, the details of which shocked a community and left trial jurors in tears Hit by Simon Richardson as he cycled home from work - before being dragged 1.3 miles under the car - Mr Mullins' life ended on a grass verge by the side of the road Horrified witnesses followed a trail of blood before finding him fatally injured. Now Mr Mullins' family - as well as colleagues, parents and children from the Trafford school - finally have justice

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tuesday 6 October 2026 at 5:15pm Zac Bolland and and his accomplice David Worrall were both given four life sentences for the petrol bombing. Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

candidates.evidence_text: Bee Network tram services are running again on all lines in Greater Manchester after two weeks of major improvement work was successfully completed on time Tram services have resumed across the Altrincham, Eccles and Trafford Park lines this morning following the completion of major track replacement work between Trafford Bar and Deansgate-Castlefield Maintenance and renewal work also took place on the Eccles line and in the city centre during a planned closure between 19 October to 1 November Engineers have replaced around 4km of track on one of the busiest and most complex sections of the network, where five Metrolink lines converge and trams pass through every 30 seconds for much of the day The new track will allow further speed restrictions to be lifted, helping to improve journey times and provide smoother, more reliable journeys for passengers. candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester has diagnosed the most lung cancers in the country as part of Lung Cancer Screening, as the NHS encourages more people to take up their lung health check when they get their invite The city is one of the first areas in England to roll out NHS lung cancer screening across all 10 of its localities, achieving the national target four years ahead of schedule New figures released at the start of Lung Cancer Awareness Month in November reveal that 1,829 lung cancers have now been diagnosed through the NHS Lung Cancer Screening Programme in Greater Manchester, with more than 80% detected at an earlier stage, giving people more treatment The targeted programme invites people registered with a GP in Greater Manchester who are aged 55 to 74 and who currently smoke or have smoked in the past for a lung health check on a mobile clinic which tours the city. Those identified as high risk are then offered a low-dose CT More than 208,738 lung health checks have now been carried out in Greater Manchester with 95,001 people going on to be referred for low dose CT Most of these people get reassurance that everything is OK but if anything is detected people are offered follow up tests or treatment

candidates.lead: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges In December 2023 a trial was launched to embed two Citizens Advice case workers in two Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) run hospitals in Manchester - the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital and North Manchester General Hospital This was further expanded in June 2024 to include Wythenshawe Hospital, and the MRI in March 2025, and St Mary's in December 2025 with funding through MFT’s charity, as well as a damp and mould focused case worker funded through Manchester City Council The team of six Citizens Advice caseworkers are aimed at providing better wrap around care for patients and addressing the link we know exists between poor health, economic hardship and housing issues The trial has been a huge success with more than 1,500 people supported across the trial locations With more up to 3m patients contacts across MFT each year this presented a huge opportunity to reach people who may otherwise have not known about the services provided by Citizens Advice, or the support they were eligible to claim

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

candidates.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

candidates.lead: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867.
candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. evidence_packet.evidence_text: L-R: Simon Shaw, Anna Dick, Alastair Brown, Tripti Anil, Alan Jackson Simon Shaw, Delivery Director at Codurance, hosted the lunchtime session for tech leaders and introduced Codurance, which is a global software engineering consultancy that has run its Manchester office for 15 years He was joined on the panel by Anna Dick, Chief Technology & Product Officer at Capsule; Alastair Brown, Group Director of AI and Technology at Peninsula; Tripti Anil, Senior Leader, Data & Analytics at Kellanova; and Alan Jackson, Director of Client Solutions at Codurance Talking about discovering how AI can be used in projects, Anna said that Capsule's initial three months of AI exploration across all its business teams built appetite for further experimentation, but it also got a little out of control. Some things needed revisiting and tidying u Alastair stressed product discipline in order to understand the business driver and the outcome you want. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. They started with UK field sales as a proof of concept initially

It looked dated, parts of it no longer worked properl The Social Bay started again from scratch, giving Northvale a fresh, confident site that finally matches the reputation behind it Engineers can find the datasheets, certificates and instructions they need in a searchable library, a quote is a click away on every page, and next-day quotes are promised at the top of each one. It’s a website that finally matches the reputation of the historic business behind i Alice Wood of Northvale Korting said: “Working with [The Social Bay] on the Northvale Korting website has been such a positive experience from start to finish… They really took the time to understand the vision and what we wanted to achieve.” Dan Cullen of The Social Bay added: “Northvale has more than 120 years of engineering behind it, and its website needed to show that. Engineers come looking for the right product, the right document and a quick quote, so we built the site around exactly that.”

candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Validator: previous publication found on 2026-11-01; plan-digest will make the final repeat decision (provisional=same_calendar_item_without_new_reader_moment, anchor=dated_event, ttl=1d). | Demoted from weekend_activities to future_announcements: earliest date 2026-11-08 is 6 days out. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits. | Selection: Outside DeepSeek ranking board (soft max 90).

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester will mark Remembrance Sunday with its annual city centre service this November Honouring the service and sacrifice of members of the Armed Forces community, the commemorative event is open to all and will take place on Sun 8 Nov at the Manchester Cenotaph in St Peter’s Square between 10.30am and 12pm At 10.30am veterans, serving military personnel and cadets, led by the Greater Manchester Police Band, will march from John Dalton Street to the Cenotaph At 10.45am, the civic procession will set off from Mount Street, accompanied by the Scots Guards Association Pipe Band, making its way to the Cenotaph ahead of the service At 10.58am, the service will begin. A two-minute silence will be observed at 11am in tribute to those who have lost their lives in conflict. The start and conclusion of the silence will be marked by the firing of a maroon Following the service, veterans, military personnel and cadets will take part in a short return march across St Peter’s Square to Mount Street

Guests can expect Spanish-inspired small plates, generously loaded focaccias, charcuterie made for sharing and a drinks list packed with wine, beer Lunchtimes at El Gatito will centre around a selection of generously loaded focaccias, served Monday to Friday from 11am – 4pm, alongside a menu of Spanish-inspired small plates Available to eat in or take away, the focaccia lineup includes the signature ‘Iberico Club’, layering jamon serrano, salchichon, chorizo, manchego, roasted peppers, tomato, lettuce and salsa verde. A vegetarian option will also be available, featuring a twist on a traditional Spa By evening, El Gatito will switch focus to tapas, sharing plates and drinks, shaped by comforting flavours from Spain and across the Mediterranean. Highlights include melt-in-the-mouth slow-cooked Beef Short Rib and smoky Catalan Chorizo, sizzling Gambas Pil Pil, Manchego Churros Interiors will be kept purposely relaxed, with green booth seating, open-plan areas and bifold doors which open directly onto a dedicated terrace

Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы.
